meta.title: PULSE-A Flight Software Hub
meta.note: Seeded from the docs site nav, a word-count scan of each page, and the IDR discrepancies sheet. Dependencies between apps (Related) were inferred from page descriptions and need team review.

appGroups.name: OBC applications
appGroups.desc: Custom apps on the On-Board Computer (cFS instance 1).

apps.name: ADCS Manager
apps.desc: Monitors the current satellite orientation and packages messages to match ADCS standards.
apps.codeNote: On main, apps/adcs_app is only a git submodule pointer to the private adcs_app repo (not read). The test_app-for-ADCS branch shows sample_app sending it sun-point and turn-from-sun commands.

apps.name: Communication Manager
apps.desc: Primary interface to the CAN bus and backup I2C bus; prevents message collisions and handles queuing and prioritization.
apps.codeNote: In code this is "bus_comms". Three divergent copies exist; the newest is on cross-compile-initial (Apr 20, 2026). See change CH-001.

apps.name: Deployment
apps.desc: Sequences deployable actions after release and instructs the ADCS to begin detumbling.

apps.name: GPS Manager
apps.desc: Interfaces with the GNSS receiver to track position and notifies other apps as the vehicle reaches ground-station overpasses.

apps.name: Payload Manager
apps.desc: Uses NASA's SBN to track the Payload Controller's state and relay key events during the PAT sequence.

apps.name: Power Manager
apps.desc: Monitors the PDU and manages power distribution and thermal control.

apps.name: Radio Manager
apps.desc: Manages radio state; queues and transmits downlink packets.
apps.codeNote: Two competing implementations on radio-manager-dev (radio_murgas_app and radio_app). See change CH-002.

apps.name: Watchdog Monitor
apps.desc: Sends heartbeats to the external watchdog timer and exchanges heartbeats with the Payload Controller so both computers stay operational, enabling fail-over if the OBC becomes unresponsive.

appGroups.name: Payload Controller applications
appGroups.desc: Second cFS instance; also runs essential OBC apps as a backup. NOTE: IDR item RID-08 asked to descope to a single computer; see Checklist.

apps.name: Data Collection
apps.desc: Logs payload data for post-pass downlink and analysis.

apps.name: FPGA Manager
apps.desc: Handles laser-modulation FPGA I/O and telemetry.

apps.name: FSM Manager
apps.desc: Performs calibration of, keeps track of the state of, and commands the fast steering mirror (FSM).

apps.name: Laser Manager
apps.desc: Tracks state and drives both the beacon and transmission lasers.

apps.name: PAT
apps.desc: Takes data from other apps and orchestrates the Pointing, Acquisition and Tracking sequence.

apps.name: Quadcell Manager
apps.desc: Processes signals from the quadrant photodiode (QPD) and provides the data transformations other apps need.

appGroups.name: NASA-provided cFS applications
appGroups.desc: Off-the-shelf cFS apps PULSE-A configures. Docs should cover how WE use and configure them.

apps.name: Checksum
apps.desc: Ensures onboard memory integrity through CRC calculations.

apps.name: CFDP
apps.desc: CCSDS File Delivery Protocol services.

apps.name: Data Store
apps.desc: Stores software bus messages in files.

apps.name: File Manager
apps.desc: Onboard file system management services.

apps.name: Health and Safety
apps.desc: Monitors application health and provides watchdog services.

apps.name: Housekeeping
apps.desc: Builds and sends combined telemetry messages.

apps.name: Limit Checker
apps.desc: Monitors telemetry against threshold limits.

apps.name: Memory Dwell
apps.desc: Monitors memory addresses accessed by the CPU.

apps.name: Memory Manager
apps.desc: Memory loading and dumping.

apps.name: SBN
apps.desc: Connects the cFE Software Bus to other buses (Software Bus Network between instances).

apps.name: Stored Commands
apps.desc: Manages autonomous command sequences.

appGroups.name: Simulation software
appGroups.desc: Used to test flight software before hardware.

apps.name: 42 Simulator
apps.desc: Spacecraft dynamics simulation (see page).

apps.name: D2S2 Simulator
apps.desc: D2S2 simulation (see page).

onboarding.welcome: Welcome to PULSE-A flight software. Work through these tracks in order; tick steps as you finish them (your progress is saved to your own account). Times are rough estimates.

tracks.name: Day 1: Understand the mission
tracks.desc: What PULSE-A is, who is on the team, and the vocabulary everyone uses. About an hour.

steps.title: Mission Overview
steps.why: 3U CubeSat, 10 Mbps space-to-ground laser link using circular polarization shift keying (CPolSK); the segments, the timeline, and what each of the 11 departments does.

steps.title: Pointing, Acquisition, and Tracking (PAT)
steps.why: The sequence the whole payload exists to perform; several flight apps (PAT, FSM, Laser, Quadcell) serve it. Study the sequence diagram.

steps.title: Reference List: definitions and acronyms
steps.why: Skim now, keep open later. Defines Payload Computer vs Payload Controller, the three lasers, and ~60 acronyms.

steps.title: System Architecture Overview
steps.why: Launch, Space and Ground segments and how subsystems interface.

steps.title: UCSP CubeSat Division page
steps.why: The public face of the project; useful to explain what you work on.

tracks.name: Week 1: Flight software foundations
tracks.desc: cFS, the software bus, Linux basics and the computers the software runs on.

steps.title: Flight Software documentation index
steps.why: Map of every FSW page, split into OBC apps, Payload Controller apps and NASA-provided apps.

steps.title: cFS General
steps.why: OSAL, PSP, cFE and the publish/subscribe model, then how PULSE-A splits apps between the OBC and the Payload Controller.

steps.title: cFS Software Bus
steps.why: Pipes, subscriptions and message IDs, with a CFE_SB_SubscribeEX code example. Most app bugs show up here.

steps.title: Operating System (Linux/Debian, SSH, SCP)
steps.why: Practice every command on the page against a Linux machine; the boards run Debian and you reach them by SSH/SCP.

steps.title: Command and Data Handling subsystem
steps.why: Two nearly identical computers (OBC and Payload Controller), dual-redundant CAN, and a private Ethernet link between them.

steps.title: On-Board Computer and Payload Controller
steps.why: BeagleBone Black on a PC/104 flight motherboard with RTC, CAN transceiver and an external MSP430 watchdog.

steps.title: Tailscale: get access to the lab devices
steps.why: Install it and sign in with the team Google account to reach the lab router and BeagleBones. Ask a lead for the account details; do not guess them.

steps.title: NASA cFS Training (Draco) slides
steps.why: The best general cFS tutorial found in the team browser tabs. Skim; do not try to finish it in one sitting.

steps.title: Download and read the cFS-simulation README
steps.why: A copy of the NASA cFS bundle. Try to build it and send a command; the README lists the steps.

tracks.name: Week 2: Buses, protocols and apps
tracks.desc: How the pieces talk, then the apps themselves.

steps.title: CAN
steps.why: The primary spacecraft bus (dual redundant).

steps.title: CSP (Cubesat Space Protocol)
steps.why: Network protocol layer used across subsystems.

steps.title: I2C
steps.why: Backup bus and sensor interface.

steps.title: SPI
steps.why: Peripheral interface.

steps.title: OBC apps: read all eight pages
steps.why: ADCS Manager, Communication Manager, Deployment, GPS Manager, Payload Manager, Power Manager, Radio Manager, Watchdog Monitor. Use the Apps tab of this hub to jump between them and see related apps.

steps.title: Payload Controller apps: read all six pages
steps.why: Data Collection, FPGA Manager, FSM Manager, Laser Manager, PAT, Quadcell Manager.

steps.title: NASA-provided apps: skim the list
steps.why: Checksum, CFDP, Data Store, File Manager, Health and Safety, Housekeeping, Limit Checker, Memory Dwell, Memory Manager, SBN, Stored Commands.

steps.title: Pick the app you want to own
steps.why: Tell a lead which app you want to own. The Apps tab marks which doc pages are thin and where code exists.

tracks.name: Week 3: Team workflow and your first contribution
tracks.desc: Access, the repos, and the first useful thing you can do.

steps.title: Get access to the UChicago-Space-Program GitHub org
steps.why: The docs say this org holds every repository and the docs themselves. Ask a lead to invite your account.

steps.title: Join #general-fsw on the PULSE Discord and fill out the UCSP headcount form
steps.why: Brian Yu's onboarding email mentions both; ask him for the invite link if you lack it.

steps.title: Read the pulse-firmware README (PayloadFPGA is the useful part)
steps.why: Holds Teensy sketches, FPGA bitstream code and test files, not the cFS code. Know what is there so you do not look for flight software in it.

steps.title: Look at cFS-flight: main, then the radio-manager-dev and cross-compile-initial branches
steps.why: main is only the NASA bundle plus PULSE-A_defs. The real app work (bus_comms, radio, CFDP) is on branches. Start with the Changes tab, then read apps/bus_comms and apps/radio_murgas_app.

steps.title: Run the end-to-end CFDP test rig (tools/radio-mock, tools/ground-station)
steps.why: Mock radio (CSP 2) and mock ground station (CSP 3) around bus_comms (CSP 1) on vcan0. The best way to see the data path work. Ask Akash Piya or the leads for the run steps; the docstrings in the scripts list the commands.

steps.title: Systems Engineering: Introduction, Requirements and Verification plans
steps.why: The SRD and V&V plan say how each requirement will be verified; CDR will check your app against them.

steps.title: IDR Review Discrepancies sheet (needs Drive access)
steps.why: What reviewers asked for. Four items touch flight software; they are on the Checklist tab.

steps.title: First contribution: expand one thin app page
steps.why: Take a page badged "thin" on the Apps tab, write its commands, telemetry, SB messages, tables, events and tests, then tick the matching Checklist item.

departments.text: Designs and builds the optical transmit terminal for CPolSK communications.
Builds the optical receive terminal on the ground.
Power distribution unit, battery board, on-board computer, and attitude control.
Command and data handling; writes and tests all flight software. (That is us.)
Satellite and ground RF hardware and software, and the RF ground station at UChicago.
Satellite geometry and the payload optomechanics.
Integration across departments and system-level tests such as environmental testing.
Grants, industry partners, sponsorships and donors.
Educational outreach and promoting the team.

terms.text: Polarization-modUlated Laser Satellite Experiment, a 3U CubeSat (per the docs mission overview).
Circular Polarization Shift Keying: bits are left and right circular polarization.
NASA Core Flight System; its Core Flight Executive; the OS Abstraction Layer; the Platform Support Package.
cFE publish/subscribe messaging between apps, using pipes and message IDs.
Software Bus Network: NASA app that bridges the bus between separate cFS instances.
On-Board Computer: BeagleBone Black on a PC/104 flight motherboard.
Board with the payload computer (BeagleBone) and payload FPGA; backup for the OBC.
Pointing, Acquisition and Tracking sequence that aligns the lasers.
Fast steering mirror / quadrant photodiode, used in the pointing loop.
Optical Ground Station / Radio Frequency Ground Station.
Buses and protocol used between computers and peripherals.
Attitude determination and control / power distribution unit / electrical power system.
System Requirements, Preliminary Design and Critical Design Reviews. Our CDR is on 2026-11-17.
Assembly, integration and testing / verification and validation / thermal vacuum chamber.
1550 nm downlink laser; 638 nm payload beacon; 1064 nm OGS beacon.

headsUp: The Mission Overview page still says CDR is in November 2025 and that launch is Q1 2027; the team's CDR is on 2026-11-17. Treat dates on that page as stale until it is updated.
The docs describe two computers (OBC and Payload Controller), but IDR item RID-08 asked to descope to one. Check the current decision before relying on the dual-computer design.
The Software Bus page URL has a typo (cFS-sfotware-bus.html). The link in this hub is the live one.

In the code, the "Communication Manager" is the app bus_comms (the FSW index title "Bus Communications Application" is the older name). The docs describe CAN plus I2C, but the code uses CSP over SocketCAN only.
The docs home says pulse-firmware holds the FSW C files. It does not: the cFS code is in cFS-flight, and pulse-firmware holds Teensy sketches, FPGA code and test files.
cFS-flight main has no PULSE-A app code of its own; the real work is spread over unmerged branches (see the Changes tab).

architecture.note: Grey edges come from the Integration Points sections of the docs pages. Maroon edges are verified in the code on the radio-manager-dev and cross-compile-initial branches. Click a box to see its interfaces, code status and the changes that affect it.

changes.title: bus_comms: the newest copy drops interfaces the radio app needs
changes.detail: cross-compile-initial (Apr 20, 2026) has the newest bus_comms, adding CAN request/response MIDs 0x1890/0x0890 and a TEST_CAN command, but its headers no longer define BUS_COMMS_SEND_CSP_CC or BUS_COMMS_CSP_RX_DATA_MID (0x088A). radio_murgas_app on radio-manager-dev includes bus_comms_msgids.h/bus_comms_msg.h and uses both, so it would not compile against the newest bus_comms. Based on header comparison; a full build was not run.
changes.action: Pick one bus_comms as canonical, keep both interface sets, then rebuild and retest the CFDP file path.

changes.title: Two radio apps with the same names and command codes
changes.detail: radio_app (AX100/ZMQ-CSP prototype, CMD MID 0x1884) and radio_murgas_app (CSP through bus_comms plus NASA CF, CMD MID 0x1886) both define RADIO_APP_* symbols, command codes 0-4 and a RADIO_APP entry point, so they cannot be linked together. Only radio_murgas_app is wired to bus_comms/CF. Neither is in any APPLIST or startup script yet.
changes.action: Decide which one survives, rename or delete the other, and document the survivor.

changes.title: Message ID overlaps (no MID allocation table)
changes.detail: ci_lab and radio_app both use 0x1884, 0x1885 and 0x0884; ci_lab is in the built APPLIST, so adding radio_app would collide. radio_murgas_app also defines RADIO_APP_TO_CSP_CAN_CONFIG/TX_MID as 0x1888/0x1889, duplicating bus_comms CMD/SEND_HK MIDs (the definitions are currently unused). The apps/ tree has 20+ MIDs picked by hand.
changes.action: Create one mission MID/topic table (this hub can host it) and assign IDs before more apps are added.

changes.title: main and the feature branches have diverged in layout
changes.detail: main renamed sample_defs to PULSE-A_defs, added a Makefile, and added apps/adcs_app as a git submodule with an SSH URL (git@github.com:...adcs_app.git, private repo). radio-manager-dev has 22 commits not on main, cross-compile-initial 14, feature/buscomms_branch 13, and none contain main's last 4. Everyone who built from sample_defs will see conflicts, and the submodule needs SSH access to a private repo.
changes.action: Agree a merge order (bus_comms, then radio, then CF), port sample_defs changes into PULSE-A_defs, and document how to get access to adcs_app.

changes.title: Dual-computer design is built into code and docs
changes.detail: targets.cmake builds cpu1 and cpu2, bus_comms picks CSP addresses from the processor ID (1 and 2), and the docs rely on SBN between OBC and Payload Controller. The SmallSat paper and RID-08 say the two computers were combined into one. If that is final, SBN, the inter-computer heartbeat and Payload Manager's PC tracking change.
changes.action: Leads confirm the single-computer decision, then update the architecture, targets.cmake and each affected page.
changes.source: SmallSat 2026 paper; IDR RID-08; cFS-flight targets.cmake

changes.title: Docs describe behaviour the code does not have
changes.detail: Communication Manager docs: CAN plus backup I2C and per-module handling for ADCS/GPS/radio/deployment. Code: CSP over SocketCAN, no I2C, only a placeholder source-to-SBN map. Radio Manager docs: UART radio, Limit Checker input, watchdog heartbeats. Code: CSP/CFDP file transfer, none of those. The docs' CFDP app is the NASA "cf" app in code. The FSW index calls the app "Bus Communications Application", which matches the code name bus_comms.
changes.action: Rewrite these pages from the code (drafts are in the vault) and mark planned features as planned.

changes.title: Most documented apps have no code in the public repos
changes.detail: 11 custom apps (Deployment, GPS Manager, Power Manager, Payload Manager, Watchdog Monitor, Data Collection, FPGA Manager, FSM Manager, Laser Manager, PAT, Quadcell Manager) and 9 NASA apps (Checksum, Data Store, File Manager, Housekeeping, Limit Checker, Memory Dwell, Memory Manager, SBN, Stored Commands) have no source in any branch checked. ADCS lives in a private repo. Last push to cFS-flight was Apr 27, 2026.
changes.action: Ask the leads where this code lives (private repos, laptops, other branches). If it does not exist, CDR docs should say "planned" for these.

changes.title: pulse-firmware is stale and mislabeled in the docs
changes.detail: The docs home says pulse-firmware holds the FSW C files. Its README says OBC and PC are Teensy boards and the OBC.ino/PC.ino sketches are empty outlines; PDU/ contains one file with the text "hello". The repo does hold useful PayloadFPGA work (TinyFPGA, and BeagleV-Fire bitstream added Apr 29-30, 2026). The cFS code is in cFS-flight.
changes.action: Fix the docs home sentence, update the README, and decide whether Teensy sketches should be archived.

changes.title: Build artifacts and vendored code committed
changes.detail: On the radio and cross-compile branches, apps/bus_comms/fsw/libcsp (libcsp 2.1) is vendored inside the app and includes build_py/ with CMakeCache.txt and a.out binaries (the radio branch alone adds 722 files / 87,917 lines). No CI workflows exist on main. The radio table struct also has a plaintext Password[32] field.
changes.action: Add .gitignore rules, use libcsp as a submodule or package, and add a CI build.

changes.title: A working end-to-end test rig already exists
changes.detail: tools/radio-mock (CSP address 2) and tools/ground-station (CSP address 3) on vcan0 plus bus_comms (CSP address 1) reproduce CFDP file transfer from the satellite to a mock ground station. Good for onboarding and a CDR demo.
changes.action: Write a run guide and make it the first onboarding exercise.

changes.title: ADCS command interface visible from the test branch
changes.detail: test_app-for-ADCS (Apr 24-27, 2026) lets sample_app send ADCS_APP_INT_CMD_MID with ADCS_SUN_POINT_CC and ADCS_TURN_FROM_SUN_CC to adcs_app. Gives two concrete commands to document, but the app itself is private.
changes.action: Get read access to adcs_app and document its MIDs and commands.
